title: Working with Files
execute:
  warning: false
---

DASCore reads many DAS formats and writes several; see [supported formats](../supported_formats.qmd). Paths may be local `pathlib.Path` objects or remote [`UPath`](https://pypi.org/project/universal-pathlib/) resources.

# Reading

Open a file with [`dc.spool`](`dascore.spool`) and index the spool to load a patch. DASCore detects the format.

```{python}
import dascore as dc

file_spool = dc.spool("examples://terra15_das_1_trimmed.hdf5")
patch = file_spool[0]
```

`dc.spool(directory)` opens every supported file below a directory as one lazy spool. Select and chunk first; arrays load only when you iterate or index:

```{python}
directory = dc.examples.spool_to_directory(dc.get_example_spool("diverse_das"))
spool = (
    dc.spool(directory)
    .select(acquisition_key="DAS2.*")
    .select(time=(..., "2022-01-01"))
    .chunk(time=2, overlap=0.5)
)

for chunk in spool:
    processed = chunk.detrend("time")
```

The first `dc.spool(directory)` creates a hidden index, `.dascore_index.sqlite3`, which stores file metadata so selections run before data is loaded. Call `spool.update()` after files change; it scans new or modified files and drops deleted ones. See the [spool tutorial](spool.qmd) for selecting and chunking, and the [index note](../notes/spool_index.qmd) for the index lifecycle.

A directory may also hold an [`.inventory` companion](inventory.qmd) describing the observing system. The index and inventory use reserved hidden names, so they are never read as data.

# Writing

Write a patch through `Patch.io`, naming the format:

```{python}
from pathlib import Path

path = Path("output_file.h5")
patch.io.write(path, "DASDAE")
round_trip = dc.spool(path)[0]
```

```{python}
#| echo: false
path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
```

[`dc.write`](`dascore.write`) does the same for a patch or a spool. Remote destinations work the same way with `UPath`:

```{python}
from upath import UPath

remote_path = UPath("memory://dascore/tutorial/output.h5")
patch.io.write(remote_path, "DASDAE")
remote_patch = dc.spool(remote_path)[0]
```

Some formats need a local, seekable file and go through a local cache; see [Working with remote patches](remote_patches.qmd). For compression, chunking, Zarr stores, XDAS files, and how readers grid stored coordinates, see [File formats in depth](file_formats.qmd).

# Scanning metadata

[`dc.scan`](`dascore.scan`) returns one [`PatchSummary`](`dascore.PatchSummary`) per patch without loading arrays.

```{python}
summary_index = 0
summary = dc.scan("examples://terra15_das_1_trimmed.hdf5")[summary_index]

print(summary.source_path)
print(summary.get_coord_summary("time").min)
```

Summaries also report `source_format`, `source_version`, and `source_patch_key`, which identify the formatter and the patch inside a multi-patch file. [`dc.scan_to_df`](`dascore.scan_to_df`) returns the same information as a dataframe.

Scan results and file-spool rows share one order, so a summary's position loads the same patch:

```{python}
source_spool = dc.spool(
    summary.source_path,
    file_format=summary.source_format,
    file_version=summary.source_version,
)
loaded = source_spool[summary_index]
```

[`dc.scan_payloads`](`dascore.scan_payloads`) returns [`PatchMeta`](`dascore.PatchMeta`) objects instead: patch metadata without the data, with full coordinates. With `snap=False`, formats that store per-sample coordinates expose their exact values. Payload scans may read large coordinate arrays, so reserve them for targeted files.

```{python}
payload = dc.scan_payloads(summary.source_path, snap=False)[0]
time = payload.coords.get_coord("time")
```

# External formats

`Patch.io` also converts patches to structures used by pandas, xarray, and ObsPy. See the [external conversion recipe](../recipes/external_conversion.qmd).
